run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:49:46Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by frontend-proxy ingress spans that end as HTTP 504 gateway timeouts (~15 s), which begin in the same minute cart starts failing to reach its Redis storage. The single traced request path (load-generator -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 -> frontend GET /api/cart 500 -> frontend -> cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, 479 s) ends in cart's own error 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis'. cart's configured Redis endpoint is valkey-cart:6379, i.e. the single endpoint pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr. Redis statistics for that pod (exported by the otel-collector redisreceiver) stop advancing at about 01:49-01:52 and stop being reported after ~01:55:50, and cart's redis client spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) decay to zero by 02:00, while other services on the same node (i-0146cb0d0caf26bae) keep serving normally. Checked alternatives do not hold up: no deployment/ReplicaSet rollout or pod restart occurred in the window, all flagd fault-injection flags are 'off', nodes report no pressure, and cart's CPU throttling rose only after the errors began. What happened inside the valkey-cart container (hang, pause, runtime stall) could not be established: the container is still 'running/ready' with 0 restarts, no last termination state, and produced no log lines in the window. Hence the conclusion is partial: the failing dependency is identified, its mechanism and trigger are not.

claims.text: For service frontend-proxy, traces_span_metrics_calls_total carries only the status_code values STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and the whole error signal comes from the span_name 'ingress' (increase 961.29 over the window; the paired 'router frontend egress' span shows 0).

frontend-proxy's 5-minute error-span rate was at background level before the alert (0/s at 01:30:50, 0.0111/s at 01:35:50, 0.0037/s at 01:40:50, 0.0111/s at 01:45:50) and then jumped to 0.567/s at 01:50:50, 1.463/s at 01:55:50 and 0.717/s at 02:00:50, while the non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) rate fell from ~20.8/s to 4.3/s over the same period.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 responses: 5 sampled error 'ingress' spans from 01:56:59-01:57:17 have http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of 14.999-15.001 s, while concurrently sampled non-error 'ingress' spans in the same traces return http.status_code=200 in 2.8-4.0 ms.

Full trace 89d64c7b2d5cbc297f9fe9426df46e75 shows load-generator 'user_view_cart' -> load-generator GET (504, 15.0 s) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (504, 15.0 s) -> frontend 'GET /api/cart' (http.status_code=500, 501.2 s) -> frontend client span 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' (rpc.grpc.status_code=9, 501.2 s) -> cart server span 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' (ERROR, 479.7 s) whose status description is 'FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected()'.

The cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' (followed by 'Error status code ... raised') repeatedly, first observed at 01:50:28.539 and continuing through 01:56:22 and beyond in the fetched slice, interleaved with normal 'GetCartAsync called with userId=...' lines.

cart's Deployment sets env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 (FLAGD_HOST=flagd), and the valkey-cart Service (port 6379) has exactly one endpoint address, pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr at 100.96.2.228; the cart Service endpoint is the single pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 at 100.96.2.233.

The Redis endpoint pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae and its container 'valkey-cart' has been running since 2026-11-18T01:16:43Z with restartCount 0, ready=true, started=true and an empty lastState.

Redis statistics scraped from valkey-cart by the otel-collector redisreceiver stop advancing: redis_memory_used_bytes is identical (1,710,360) at 01:49:46 and 01:54:46, the rate of redis_cpu_time_seconds_total drops to exactly 0 at 01:52:46 and stays 0 at 01:54:46 and 01:56:46, and redis_memory_peak_bytes is frozen at 1,726,344 from 01:54:46; over the authorised window these redis_* series only carry samples between roughly 01:29:46 and 01:55:50.

cart's own Redis client spans decay to zero during the incident: 10-minute increases of HGET are 3313.7 at 01:40:00, 3207.4 at 01:50:00, 1931.6 at 01:52:00, 1402.1 at 01:54:00, 789.5 at 01:56:00, 102.1 at 01:58:00 and 0 from 02:00:00 onward (HMSET and EXPIRE follow the same curve).

cart's server-side span p95 for 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' is pinned at 15000 ms (top histogram bucket) from 01:52:46 through 02:00:46, whereas cart's redis client spans HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE kept p95 values of about 1.9-73.7 ms while they still had data (through ~01:54:46).

Error-status spans in the window belong to cart (84.0), frontend (256.4), frontend-proxy (961.3) and checkout (13.5); cart's errors are on 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' (45.23) and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' (38.77), frontend's on 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart', 'POST /api/checkout', the /api/cart and /api/checkout route spans and the grpc CartService/CheckoutService client spans, and checkout's on 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder'.

All fault-injection settings in flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) are off: cartFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure have defaultVariant 'off'; emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage have defaultVariant 'off' (value 0).

No rollout or restart occurred inside the window: all 21 otel-demo Deployments report availableReplicas=1, readyReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1, every ReplicaSet was created at 01:16:34-01:18:20 (before the first failure), and every otel-demo pod is Ready with restartCount 0.

Node conditions show no resource pressure: all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure=False at their last heartbeats between 01:51:19Z and 01:55:51Z, including node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (heartbeat 01:54:07Z).

An old cart pod, cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s, was part of a 'Killing' event at 01:52:36Z and the kubelet logged a Warning FailedKillPod at 01:52:35Z ('rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded' for KillContainer and KillPodSandbox); that pod is not an endpoint of the cart Service (which lists only cart-755465879b-t9mf7) and its container showed a CPU throttled-period fraction of exactly 0 for every sample in the window.

cart's container CPU throttled-period fraction rose from ~0.17-0.23 (01:28:46-01:50:46) to 0.44 at 01:52:46, 0.74 at 01:54:46, 0.83 at 01:56:46 and 0.88-0.90 at 01:58:46-02:00:46, while valkey-cart's stayed between 0.016 and 0.066 and valkey-cart's CPU usage was only ~0.0022-0.0035 cores (limit 10m).
Memory stayed far below limits: the cart pod's working set grew from ~57 MB to ~95 MB (limit 165Mi) around 01:52-02:00, and valkey-cart's stayed at ~3.6-4.0 MB (limit 10Mi) with no restart.

Several services that share node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae with cart and valkey-cart kept serving without error-status spans: product-catalog (17470 non-error spans, one sampled GetProduct span returning rpc.grpc.status_code=0 in 96-143 µs), quote (2136), shipping (2133), currency (2039), email (2868), image-provider (183); accounting and payment have error series with increase 0.

The valkey-cart pod's Kubernetes status is not a health signal here: the container is 'running' and 'ready' only because the pod defines no readiness/liveness probe (the Deployment spec lists no probes), and the container emitted zero log lines in the window, so pod status alone cannot show it was serving.

The valkey-cart Redis endpoint (pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, service valkey-cart:6379) stopped serving at about 01:49-01:50, which is why cart's EnsureRedisConnected fails and why cart's GetCart/AddItem calls hang; support: cart's first connection failure at 01:50:28 coincides with valkey's memory/cpu/peak statistics freezing, the collector's redis scrape then disappears, and both cart (node i-0146) and the otel-collector (node i-0a709b85c49d987be) lose their Redis signal at the same time.

The mechanism that stopped the valkey-cart container from serving is not visible in this data: the process was not restarted (restartCount 0, startedAt 01:16:43Z), was not OOM-capped or CPU-starved by its own container metrics (0.002-0.0035 cores of a 10m limit, 3.6-4.0 MB of a 10Mi limit, throttled-periods fraction under 0.07), had no probe to fail, and wrote no logs, so a hung/paused Redis process versus a runtime or network-path stall cannot be distinguished from the evidence available.

An alternative remaining candidate is name resolution or the network path from cart to valkey-cart: cart's client message 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' also covers a failed endpoint resolution, and no DNS signal was available to test it (payment's dns.lookup/tcp.connect spans recorded 0 calls in the window, and no CoreDNS logs were read).

cart CPU throttling as the primary cause: throttling was still ~0.17-0.23 before the first connection failures and only climbed after 01:52:46, cart's redis client spans were still completing in single-digit-to-tens of milliseconds until ~01:54:46, and the independent otel-collector redis scrape also stopped - so throttling looks like back-pressure from hung requests rather than the trigger.

flagd fault injection (e.g. cartFailure) as the cause: every fault flag in flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off', and the failure cart reports is a genuine Redis connection exception from ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(), not a synthetic cart failure.

A rollout, restart or pod replacement of cart or valkey-cart inside the window as the cause: all Deployments are fully available, every ReplicaSet predates the incident (01:16:34-01:18:20), and both the cart and valkey-cart containers report restartCount 0 with no last termination state.

Node-level failure or resource pressure on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (which hosts cart and valkey-cart) as the cause: the node reports Ready with no memory, disk or PID pressure at 01:54:07Z, and other pods on that node (product-catalog, quote, shipping, checkout's non-cart paths, frontend-proxy itself) kept serving.

Verify the valkey-cart container directly: run a Redis PING/INFO against 100.96.2.228:6379 from the cart pod, inspect the containerd/kubelet state of container valkey-cart on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, and check whether the process is paused/SIGSTOPped or blocked (e.g. on a fork or the emptyDir volume), since the deployed pod has no probes and writes no logs.

Add a readiness/liveness probe (redis-cli ping) and low-level logging to the valkey-cart container so that a hung Redis instance becomes visible in pod status instead of only through caller errors and the collector's redisreceiver; also consider raising the container's 10m CPU / 10Mi memory limits, which leave no headroom for fork-based persistence.

gaps: Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so what changed at ~01:49-01:50 (if anything) cannot be determined.

The valkey-cart container produced no log lines: the log query for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr returned no data for 01:30-02:05:50 and for its default window, so there is no server-side evidence of why Redis stopped serving.

Kubernetes NetworkPolicy state could not be corroborated: the networkpolicies query over the whole cluster matched nothing (no_data), and the cilium-agent pod on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae returned no matching log lines, so whether a policy or datapath drop blocked cart->valkey-cart traffic is unknown.
kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_*, kube_.*) returned no names in the window, so pod-phase/restart metrics could not corroborate the object status snapshots.

No DNS signal was available: payment's dns.lookup and tcp.connect spans recorded 0 calls in the window and no CoreDNS logs were read, so a name-resolution failure as the cause of 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' remains unchecked rather than excluded.

The instant query for redis_memory_used_bytes at 02:05:50 returned no data and container network/fs metrics did not exist under the queried names, so redis traffic and disk activity during 01:55-02:05 could not be observed.

What this alert caused downstream of the demo (load-generator 504s aside) was not verified; the load-generator's own trace shows one http.status_code=504 GET but its error rate was not read from metrics.
next_steps: Inspect the valkey-cart container state and runtime logs on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (containerd/CRI logs around 01:49-01:50) to explain the frozen Redis statistics.
Compare against a pre-incident baseline of Redis ops/connection counts to confirm the endpoint itself stopped accepting connections rather than cart's client being isolated.
Review change records for otel-demo around 01:49 (change history integration is missing in this Run).

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then.
